chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And let not the witnesses refuse when they are summoned.' He said: 'It is not fitting for anyone, when summoned to give testimony upon which he is testifying, to say: I do not testify to you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a witness refusing to testify when summoned according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the obligation of testimony by interpreting the phrase 'do not refuse' in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:282 as a prohibition against a summoned witness refusing to testify. This establishes the legal principle that once called upon, a witness is bound to provide evidence, reinforcing the communal duty of truthfulness in judicial matters. The ruling underscores the seriousness of withholding testimony, linking it directly to the divine command in the verse.
